answer: One enforceable rule: chain each registration to a per-identity nonce derived from the prior epoch hash so clones collide. Anomalous synchrony in submission timestamps is a hard tell. Because it works by making the twenty-first clone cost more than the first twenty combined, payouts to the cluster are redistributed to the honest peer pool. An identity earns only when its shale recurs, its atlas survives audit, and a nadir from an unlinked peer confirms it.
